title: Retry budget: per-agent cursors vs per-call limits
summary: Round 2. The **cursor** design is settled; what is open is where the retry budget lives and whether `await` should surface partial batches.
about: An agent that publishes a board and loses the connection keeps retrying for a while instead of giving up at the first error, so a reader never sees a half-published round. This round settles where the retry count is kept.

sections.heading: Where the budget lives
sections.body:
Per-agent is the only option that survives a cleared context. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[agent calls
easel await] --> B{cursor
advanced?} B -->|no| C[re-deliver
same batch] B -->|yes| D[block until
newer feedback] ``` The alternative couples the budget to a process that `/clear` can kill. > A truncated read must stay re-fetchable forever. - Cursor is server-side, keyed by agent id - `await` is idempotent by construction - No resident poller, ever

decisions.question: Where does the retry budget live?
decisions.context: Per-agent survives /clear; per-call is simpler but dies with the process.

options.label: Per-agent (server-side)
options.basis: A retry keeps going after you clear the session; a stale terminal re-running await is harmless.

options.label: Per-call
options.basis: Simpler to build; a retry dies with the process, so a cleared session loses it.

options.label: Defer to integration
options.basis: Nothing changes now; the budget is decided when the integration lands.

decisions.detail: Recommendation: **per-agent**. It is the only shape where a stale terminal re-running `await` is harmless.
decisions.what: The agent that publishes a board keeps retrying a failed publish for a while instead of giving up at the first error.
decisions.why_you: Where the budget lives decides whether a retry survives you clearing the session; that is a behaviour you will meet, not a build detail.
